newsitem.title: USA: GTE cuts back 97 growth forecasts to nearly flat.
newsitem.headline: GTE cuts back 97 growth forecasts to nearly flat.

text.p: GTE Corp said it expects 1997 growth to be lower-than-expected after the local phone service set a four-point strategy to establish itself as a provider of local, long distance, Internet and wireless services with an advanced fiber optic network.
GTE said it expects earnings per share growth to be "flat to slgihtly positive" in a release and in a meeting with security analysts.
The company had previously said it expected earnings growth of not less than 10 percent.

GTE said the short-term reduction was a results of the plan under which it will acquire BBN Corp for $616 million, buy a coast-to-coast fiber optic network, set up a pact with networking company Cisco Systems Inc to develop the network, and will create a business unit to market its integrated voice, video and data solutions.

"In 1998, we see moderate growth in EPS and in 1999 and beyond, we're looking for a growth rate that is 30 to 50 percent higher than our previous guidance of not less than 10 percent," said Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Lee in the release.
